FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finanzed by the Automotive Electrical Equipments and Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division CounciL For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical-values (revised'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1S 15730:2006

Indian Standard
ac FLASHERS

FOR 2 AND 3 WHEELERS

1 SCOPE This standard specifies requirements and methods of tests for solid state ac flashers with a load of two lamps for direction indicators of automotive having a regulated 12V ac (rms) system. The flashing of direction indicating lamps on the same side of the vehicle shall occur alternately or synchronously. Hot wires type flashers with a load of two lamps for direction indicators of automotive having a 6 V, 12 V and 24 V direct current (de) system are covered in IS 4060 : 1994 `Automotive vehicles -- Flashers for direction indicators -- Specification (second revision)'. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions, which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: IS No. 1248 (Part 1) : 2003 fitle Direct acting indicating analogue electrical measuring instruments and their accessories: Part 1 Definitions and general requirements ~ourth revision) Specification for severities for environmental tests for automotive electrical equipments

switch is actuated. Secondary fimction may include the visible pilot indication for turn signal system rind an audible signal to indicate the flasher operation. The ac flasher must operate with the ac supply available on board. 3.3 Routine Tests -- Tests carried out on each ac flasher to check the parameters, which are likely to vary during production. 3.4 Type Tests -- Tests carried out to prove conformity with the specification. These are intended to verifi the design characteristics of a given type of ac flasher. 3.5 Acceptance Test -- Tests carried out on ac flashers taken from a lot for the purpose of acceptance of the lot. 4 DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION 4.1 The flasher shall have such a construction that if, the filament of either of the two bulbs of the.direction indicator is broken, the driver of the vehicle shall be made aware suitably. 4.1.1 Flasher shall be so designed ensuring that the failure of the direction indicator lamp is indicated as given in Table 1. Table 1 Failure of Direction Indicator Lamp Indications Magneto System (with Tnrn Pilot Indication)
a) The other direction indicating lamps shall continue to flash The frequency of flashing of the flasher in this condition should be 130 to 200 flashes-per minute The turn pilot indicator lamp shall remain glowing continuously or shows at least 20 percent change in frequency I

10250:1982

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard the following definitions shall apply. 3,1 Direction Indicator -- A lighting device to show in which direction the driver intends to turn by giving a flashing light on that side of the vehicle towards which the turn is being made, The definition does not include: a) Switchgear, and b) Semaphore type indicators. 3.2 Flasher (Flasher Unit � a c Operation)-- A device installed in a vehicle lighting system, which has the primary function of causing the direction indicator unit to flash intermittently at a specified frequency, when the turn signal 1

Rear or Front

b)

c)

4.2 The ac flasher should be so designed that it operates properly without failure for the following type of input ac waveforms: a) Sine wave, and b) Square wave. 4.3 The material used and workmanship in the construction of flashers shall be of such quality that provides adequate

IS 15730:2006 protection, in normal use, against mechanical and electrical failures and shall withstand the effects of changing weather conditions, water or excessive dampness, corrosion, dust, oil, high temperature or any other deleterious influence to which they may exposed under conditions of their normal use. 5 TESTS 5.1 Classification 5.1.1 Type Tests The following shall constitute type tests: a) Visual examination b) Performance (see 5.2); test (see 5.3); 5.2 Visual Examination Flashers shal! be examined for finish and workmanship. The flashers including their terminals shall be free from injurious flaws and visual defects. 5.3 Performance Test of Tests a) Visual examination b) Performance (see 5.2),

test (see 5.3), and

c) Life test (see-5.5). The number of samples for acceptance tests shall be agreed upon between the purchaser and the manufacturer. The flashing rate shall be measured over a period of one.minute. In case of one bulb failure condition the flashing rate shall increased to 130 to 200 flashes per minute. 5.3.4 The ratio `Time ON' to `Total cycle time' (Duty cycle) shall be 35 to 65 percent. The `OFF' period shall then permit each lamp to fall to within O to 10 percent of its fill design brilliance. 5.3.5 The time required before the flasher begins to work shall be not more than one second. 5.3.6 The voltage drop between input and output terminals of the ac flasher unit shall be less than 3.0 V 2

If, in repeat test(s) no failure occurs, the test requirement maybe considered to have been complied. 5.1.2 Acceptance Tests

ANNEX A (C/atfse 5. 1.2)
RECOMMENDED A-1 GENERAL If statistical quality control techniques have been used for production control such test results and relevant charts may be made available along with the material supplied to enable the purchaser to judge the acceptability, or otherwise ofa lot. In case such information is not available, the following procedure is recommended for judging conformity of a lot with the requirements of this standard. A-2 SCALE OF SAMP-LING A-3 NUMBER A-2.1 Lot In any consignment, all the flashers of the same rating and from the same batch of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. A-2.2 The number of flashers to be selected from a 101 shall depend upon the lot size and shall be in accordance with co] 2 and 3 of Tables 5 and 6. 6 OF TESTS AI1 the flashers selected under A-2.2 shall be subjected to acceptance tests given in 5.1.2. A-4 CRITE-RION FOR CONFORMITY PLAN OF SAMPLING A-2.3 These flashers shall be selected at random. In order to ensure randomness, the following procedure may be adopted: Arrange the flashers in a systematic manner and starting from any flasher count them as 1, 2, .... etc, up ton r being equal to the integral part of N/n, N being the lot size and n the sample size. Every rth flasher shall be included in the sample

A lot shall be considered as conforming to this standard, if the number of defects does not exceed the corresponding number given in Tables 5 and 6.
